<section_guide number="4" title="Key Features and Behavior" references="2,3">
<purpose>Describe each approved Feature as a complete, observable user behavior for the PoC.</purpose>

<required_review>
Read Section 2 to recover the complete F1, F2... list and Section 3 to recover the Primary User
Scenario. Every Feature in Section 2.2 must have exactly one 4.x entry.
</required_review>

<workflow>
Atomic confirmation is the default. Work through the Feature list in ID order.

For each Feature:

1. Ask what the user is trying to achieve and when the Feature is available.
2. Draft the ordered user actions and visible product responses.
3. Ask whether any input, limit, permission, visibility, ordering, uniqueness, allowed state, or
   forbidden change must not be left to the builder.
4. Define one observable completion checkpoint. Add states and exceptions only when the PoC must
   show or validate them.
5. Present one plain-text approval digest for the complete Feature.
6. Save one Feature with save_alps_section(4, "x", "Fx: Feature name", content).

Keep all 4.x.1-4.x.6 content in the same Feature save unit. Never split by implementation layer.
If the Feature contains independently demonstrable user outcomes, offer up to three behavioral
splits and allow the user to keep the original.
</workflow>

<approval_digest>
Include user value, confirmed scope, starting conditions, mandatory information, every applicable
product rule and value, and the completion checkpoint. Include non-goals, states, exceptions, and
failure or recovery results only when the user confirmed that they affect the PoC. Never save a
rule absent from the digest or omit a confirmed rule as a later edge case.
</approval_digest>

<completion required="true">Complete and save every Feature from Section 2.2 as its own 4.x entry.</completion>
</section_guide>
